name: Quad-core SoC with external memory: four S-mode cores, Sv32 MMU per core, instruction caches, AXI4 memory, CLINT, PLIC, UART

blocks.name: mem_arb
blocks.description: Arbiter and sequencer of the memory transactions of four harts. req0 .. req3 say which harts ask for something and kind0 .. kind3 (2 bits each) what: 00 a data access of the hart's core, 01 a page-table read, 10 an instruction-line refill; kind 11 is treated as no request. A hart is eligible when its req is 1 and its kind is not 11. Held state: state (3 bits: 0 idle, 1 read wait, 2 write wait, 3 atomic-read wait, 4 atomic decide, 5 atomic-write wait), cur (2 bits, the hart being served), core (1 bit, 1 when the hart being served asks for a data access of its core) and last (2 bits); at reset state is 0, cur 0, core 0 and last 3. The picked hart w is the first eligible one in the order last+1, last+2, last+3, last (each modulo 4); there is none when no hart is eligible. kw is the kind of w. is_ram is 1 when the data access of the picked hart is in RAM (otherwise it is in a device), c_store is 1 for a store, c_amo for an atomic instruction, c_dmem_we is 1 when the atomic instruction writes memory; all four describe the data access on the bus. eng_ready is 1 when the memory engine is idle and eng_done is 1 in the cycle a transaction completes. State 0 (idle): sel<k> is 1 for k equal to w and 0 for every other hart (all 0 when there is no w); bsel<k> is sel<k> AND kw is 00. cstore is kw 00 AND is_ram AND c_store AND NOT c_amo; camo is kw 00 AND is_ram AND c_amo; cload is kw 00 AND is_ram AND NOT c_store AND NOT c_amo; dev is kw 00 AND NOT is_ram. start is (cstore OR camo OR cload OR kw 01 OR kw 10) AND eng_ready AND w exists. eng_start is start; eng_we is start AND cstore; eng_line is start AND kw 10; eng_src (2 bits) is kw (00 when there is no w). grant<w> is 1 when dev is 1 (the access of a device completes at once); every other grant is 0. rdone and wdone are 0. On the clock edge: when start is 1, cur and last become w, core becomes 1 when kw is 00 and 0 otherwise, and state becomes 2 when cstore is 1, else 3 when camo is 1, else 1; when dev is 1 (and start is 0), last becomes w. State 1: sel<k> is 1 for k equal to cur; bsel<k> is sel<k> AND core; grant<cur> is eng_done; rdone is eng_done; wdone is 0; eng_start, eng_we, eng_line are 0 and eng_src is 00; on the edge, when eng_done is 1, state becomes 0. State 2: as state 1 except rdone is 0 and wdone is eng_done. State 3: sel and bsel as in state 1; no grant; rdone is eng_done; wdone 0; eng_start, eng_we, eng_line 0, eng_src 00; when eng_done is 1, state becomes 4. State 4: sel and bsel as in state 1; eng_start and eng_we are c_dmem_we AND eng_ready; eng_line is 0; eng_src is 00; grant<cur> is NOT c_dmem_we; rdone and wdone are 0; on the edge, state becomes 5 when c_dmem_we AND eng_ready is 1, becomes 0 when c_dmem_we is 0, else stays 4. State 5: sel and bsel as in state 1; grant<cur> is eng_done; wdone is eng_done; rdone is 0; eng_start, eng_we, eng_line 0, eng_src 00; when eng_done is 1, state becomes 0. States 6 and 7: everything is 0 and state becomes 0 on the edge. Outputs are combinational from the held state and the inputs; only the held state changes on the edge.

blocks.name: rsp_hold
blocks.description: Holds the last memory response. line (256 bits) is the memory's response, valid in a cycle when done is 1. data (256 bits) is line when done is 1, else the held value. word is bits 31:0 of data. Held state: held (256 bits), 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge, after reset, when done is 1, held becomes line.

blocks.name: sm_ptw
blocks.description: Combinational. y (32 bits) is the OR of d<k> AND (all 32 bits replicated from sel<k>) for k from 0 to 3: the input of the hart whose select is 1, and the bitwise OR of the inputs whose selects are 1 when more than one is, and 0 when no select is 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: sm_if
blocks.description: Combinational. y (32 bits) is the OR of d<k> AND (all 32 bits replicated from sel<k>) for k from 0 to 3: the input of the hart whose select is 1, and the bitwise OR of the inputs whose selects are 1 when more than one is, and 0 when no select is 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: bm_amo
blocks.description: Combinational. y is the OR over k from 0 to 3 of (sel<k> AND d<k>). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: eng_src_mux
blocks.description: Combinational. y (32 bits) is a when src (2 bits) is 00, b when src is 01, c when src is 10, and 0 when src is 11. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: zeros
blocks.description: Combinational. z1 is 0 (1 bit), z4 is 0 (4 bits), z32 is 0 (32 bits). A constant source for tying unused inputs. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: dc_wp
blocks.description: Combinational. en is 1 when run is 1 and stall is 0, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: axi_m
blocks.description: AXI4 master: word read, 32-byte line read, word write

blocks.name: bus_mux4
blocks.description: Combinational. The shared bus of four cores. grant0 .. grant3 are one bit each and at most one is 1. For each name in addr, store_data, memtype, memsrc, valid, xcpt, memwrite, kill, dmem_we and dmem_wdata the output is the input with that name and the number of the core whose grant is 1 (addr0 .. addr3 give addr, and so on); when no grant is 1, every output is 0. Widths: addr, store_data and dmem_wdata 32 bits, memtype 3, memsrc 2, the others 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: region_decode
blocks.description: Combinational address decoder for the data side, in the memory stage. addr is the 32-bit address of an access. There are six regions that do not overlap, and every other address belongs to none. The RAM is the 64 MB from 80000000 to 83FFFFFF hexadecimal: bits 31:26 of addr are 100000. The CLINT is the 64 KB from 02000000 to 0200FFFF: bits 31:16 of addr are 0000001000000000. The PLIC is the 64 MB from 0C000000 to 0FFFFFFF: bits 31:26 of addr are 000011. The UART is the 4 KB from 10000000 to 10000FFF: bits 31:12 of addr are 00010000000000000000. The peripherals are the 64 KB from 10010000 to 1001FFFF: bits 31:16 of addr are 0001000000000001. The GPU is the 32 MB from 30000000 to 31FFFFFF: bits 31:25 of addr are 0011000. For instance 84000000 (just past the RAM) and 10001000 (just past the UART) is in no region, 10010000 is a peripheral, 31FFFFFC is the GPU and 32000000 is in no region. sel_ram, sel_clint, sel_plic, sel_uart, sel_periph and sel_gpu are 1 for the region addr is in and 0 otherwise; is_io is 1 when addr is in the CLINT, PLIC, UART, peripheral or GPU region. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: bus_ctl
blocks.description: Combinational. The write and read strobes of the data-side regions, in the memory stage. sel_ram, sel_clint, sel_plic, sel_uart, sel_periph and sel_gpu say which region the access is in (at most one is 1). memwrite is 1 for a store that is really going to happen. ram_we, clint_we, plic_we, uart_we, periph_we and gpu_we are 1 when memwrite is 1 and the matching select is 1, 0 otherwise. memsrc is the write-back source of the instruction in the memory stage: a load is memsrc 01. valid is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage is a real one, xcpt is 1 when it has raised an exception and kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back this cycle. A device read happens only when memsrc is 01, valid is 1, xcpt is 0 and kill is 0: plic_re, uart_re, periph_re and gpu_re are 1 when that holds and sel_plic, sel_uart, sel_periph or sel_gpu respectively is 1, and 0 otherwise. idle (1 bit) is 1 when the memory engine is idle. The device strobes clint_we, plic_we, uart_we, periph_we, gpu_we, plic_re, uart_re, periph_re and gpu_re are also 0 whenever idle is 0 (a device is only touched while the engine is idle); ram_we does not depend on idle. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: clint_decode4
blocks.description: Combinational. Names the register of a four-hart CLINT (the layout of QEMU's virt machine) that an address picks. Only bits 15:2 of addr (the word, w) are used. kind (3 bits) and hart (2 bits): kind 1 (msip) and hart w when w is 0 to 3 (offsets 0000 to 000C hexadecimal); kind 2 (mtimecmp, low word) and kind 3 (mtimecmp, high word) with hart (w - 1000 hexadecimal) / 2 when w is 1000 to 1007 hexadecimal (offsets 4000 to 401C), low for an even w and high for an odd w; kind 4 (mtime, low word) and hart 0 when w is 2FFE hexadecimal (offset BFF8); kind 5 (mtime, high word) and hart 0 when w is 2FFF (offset BFFC); kind 0 and hart 0 for every other w. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: clint4
blocks.description: Core-local interruptor for four harts. kind (3 bits) and hart (2 bits) name the register an access picks: kind 1 is msip of hart <hart> (bit 0 only; other bits read 0 and ignore writes), kinds 2 and 3 are the low and high words of mtimecmp of hart <hart> (64 bits), kinds 4 and 5 are the low and high words of mtime (64 bits, one for all harts; hart is ignored), kinds 0, 6 and 7 name no register, which reads 0 and ignores writes. we is 1 for a store, with wdata the word stored. rdata is the register the access names before this cycle's write (0 when none); it depends only on kind, hart and the held state. At reset every msip is 0, mtime is 0, a 4-bit prescaler counter pre is 0 and every mtimecmp is all ones. On each rising clock edge, after reset: when we is 1 the register named is written (msip from wdata bit 0, a half of a mtimecmp or of mtime from wdata); and pre goes up by one (wrapping from 15 to 0) on every edge, and mtime goes up by one (wrapping at 64 bits) only on an edge where pre is 15 before the edge, except on an edge with a store to either half of mtime: that half becomes wdata, the other half keeps its value and mtime does not count (pre still counts). msip0 .. msip3 are the held msip bits. mtip<h> is 1 when the 64-bit unsigned mtime is greater than or equal to the 64-bit mtimecmp of hart h, as held (before this edge), and 0 otherwise. mtime (output, 64 bits) shows the held mtime.

blocks.name: uart16550
blocks.description: A 16550-style UART with a byte interface and a 16-byte receive FIFO, the register layout NuttX's 16550 driver, Linux's 8250 driver and QEMU's virt machine use, one byte per register. addr is the 32-bit address of an access; bits 2:0 pick the register. we is 1 for a store, with wdata bits 7:0 the byte stored; re is 1 for a load that will really happen. Held state, all 0 at reset: the interrupt enable register IER (4 bits), the line control register LCR (8 bits; its bit 7 is the divisor latch access bit, DLAB), the modem control register MCR (5 bits), the scratch register SCR (8 bits), the divisor latch low byte DLL and high byte DLM (8 bits each), the FIFO-enabled flag FE, the transmit-empty interrupt flag TXF, the overrun flag OE, and the receive FIFO: sixteen bytes of storage (numbered 0 to 15), a read position RP (4 bits), a write position WP (4 bits) and the count RXCNT (5 bits, 0 to 16, the number of bytes in the FIFO). The byte at the front of the FIFO is the storage byte numbered RP; the FIFO is empty when RXCNT is 0. Reads: rdata has the byte in bits 7:0 and 0 in bits 31:8, and depends only on addr and the held state. Offset 0 reads DLL when DLAB is 1; when DLAB is 0 it reads the front byte when RXCNT is not 0, and 0 when RXCNT is 0. Offset 1 reads DLM when DLAB is 1 and IER (bits 7:4 are 0) when DLAB is 0. Offset 2 reads the interrupt identification register: bit 0 is 0 when an interrupt is pending and 1 when none is; bits 3:1 are 010 when the receive interrupt is pending, otherwise 001 when the transmit interrupt is pending, otherwise 000; bits 5:4 are 0; bits 7:6 are 11 when FE is 1 and 00 otherwise. Offset 3 reads LCR. Offset 4 reads MCR (bits 7:5 are 0). Offset 5 reads the line status register: bit 0 is 1 when RXCNT is not 0, bit 1 is OE, bits 5 and 6 are 1 (the transmitter is always empty), every other bit is 0. Offset 6 reads 0 (the modem status register). Offset 7 reads SCR. The receive interrupt is pending when IER bit 0 is 1 and RXCNT is not 0. The transmit interrupt is pending when IER bit 1 is 1 and TXF is 1. irq is 1 when the receive interrupt or the transmit interrupt is pending. tx_valid is 1 and tx_data is wdata bits 7:0 in a cycle when we is 1, addr bits 2:0 are 0 and DLAB is 0 (a byte to transmit); otherwise tx_valid is 0 and tx_data is 0; they depend only on the inputs and the held state. On each rising clock edge, when rst is 1 everything held becomes 0 (the sixteen storage bytes too); otherwise these happen in this order, a later one overriding an earlier one for the same state. (1) Reads: when re is 1 and addr bits 2:0 are 0 and DLAB is 0 and RXCNT is not 0, the front byte is removed: RP becomes RP + 1 (modulo 16) and RXCNT becomes RXCNT - 1; when re is 1 and addr bits 2:0 are 5, OE becomes 0; when re is 1 and addr bits 2:0 are 2 and the interrupt identification register (as read this cycle) has bits 3:1 equal to 001, TXF becomes 0. (2) Stores, by addr bits 2:0 when we is 1: offset 0 with DLAB 1 writes DLL; offset 0 with DLAB 0 transmits the byte and sets TXF to 1; offset 1 with DLAB 1 writes DLM; offset 1 with DLAB 0 writes IER (low 4 bits) and, when that write takes IER bit 1 from 0 to 1, sets TXF to 1; offset 2 sets FE to wdata bit 0 and, when wdata bit 1 is 1, empties the receive FIFO (RP, WP and RXCNT become 0); offset 3 writes LCR; offset 4 writes MCR (low 5 bits); offset 7 writes SCR; stores to offsets 5 and 6 change nothing. (3) Receive: when rx_valid is 1 and RXCNT (as the steps above left it) is less than 16, the byte rx_data is stored at the storage byte numbered WP, WP becomes WP + 1 (modulo 16) and RXCNT becomes RXCNT + 1; when rx_valid is 1 and RXCNT is 16, OE becomes 1 and the byte is lost.

blocks.name: io_mux
blocks.description: Combinational. y is clint_rdata when sel_clint is 1, plic_rdata when sel_plic is 1, uart_rdata when sel_uart is 1, periph_rdata when sel_periph is 1, gpu_rdata when sel_gpu is 1, and 0 when none of the five is 1. At most one select is 1 at a time. All data are 32 bits. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: hart_cfg
blocks.description: Combinational. The configuration of four harts. meip is the PLIC's external interrupt (1 bit). meip0 is meip and meip1, meip2 and meip3 are 0 (the PLIC serves hart 0). hartid0 is 0, hartid1 is 1, hartid2 is 2 and hartid3 is 3 (2 bits each). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: plic4
blocks.description: Interrupt controller for four harts, with five level-triggered sources (s1, s2, s3, s4, s5; source numbers 1 to 5) and eight contexts (context 2h is the machine external interrupt of hart h and context 2h plus 1 is the supervisor external interrupt of hart h, h from 0 to 3). Held state, all 0 at reset: prio of each source (3 bits), enable of each context (a 6-bit mask, bit s is source s; bit 0 is always 0), threshold of each context (3 bits), and in_service of each source (1 bit). eligible(c, s) is 1 when s_s is 1, in_service of s is 0, bit s of enable of c is 1, and prio of s is greater than the threshold of c. claim(c) is the number of the eligible source of context c with the highest prio (the lowest number on a tie), or 0 when none is eligible. meip0 to meip3 and seip0 to seip3: meip<h> is 1 when claim(2h) is not 0 and seip<h> is 1 when claim(2h plus 1) is not 0 (this cycle, from the held state and s1 to s5). The registers are named by off, the word offset: bits 25:2 of addr (32 bits; the layout of the SiFive PLIC; the other bits of addr are ignored): off 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are prio of that source; off 400 hexadecimal is the pending word (bit s is s_s AND NOT in_service of s; bit 0 and bits 31:6 are 0); off 800 hexadecimal + 20 hexadecimal * c is enable of context c (bit s of the word, bits 5:1; the other bits read 0); off 80000 hexadecimal + 400 hexadecimal * c is threshold of context c; off 80001 hexadecimal + 400 hexadecimal * c is the claim register of context c (c is 0 to 7). rdata (32 bits) is the register named by off as it is held now, zero-extended (the claim register gives claim(c)); it is 0 for every other off, and it does not depend on we or re. On each rising clock edge: rst is 1: every register becomes 0. Otherwise, when we is 1: a write to off 1 to 5 sets that prio to wdata bits 2:0; a write to the enable word of c sets enable of c to wdata bits 5:1 (bit 0 stays 0); a write to the threshold word of c sets threshold of c to wdata bits 2:0; a write to the claim register of c with wdata equal to 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 clears in_service of that source; every other write changes nothing. When we is 0 and re is 1 and off is the claim register of c and claim(c) is not 0, in_service of claim(c) becomes 1 (the claim). At most one of we and re is 1.

blocks.name: wlane
blocks.description: Combinational. A store's bytes on their lanes of a 32-bit word, with byte enables (bit k of be for bits 8k+7:8k). memtype (3 bits): 000 and 011 a byte, 001 and 100 a half-word, 101 no access, 010, 110 and 111 a word. With a = bits 1:0 of addr: a byte: be has only bit a set and data is bits 7:0 of wdata shifted left by 8 times a; a half-word: with h = bit 1 of addr, be is 0011 when h is 0 and 1100 when h is 1, and data is bits 15:0 of wdata shifted left by 16 times h; a word: be is 1111 and data is wdata; no access: be and data are 0. Bits of data not on an enabled lane are 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ram_main
blocks.description: External memory model: 64 MB, AXI4 slave, 30 cycles read latency

blocks.name: postw
blocks.description: Posted plain stores: lets the core go on as soon as a plain store to RAM has been handed to the memory engine, instead of when the engine has finished it (the engine keeps the address and the data). start, we and amo are the engine's start, write and atomic flags for the transaction that is starting in this cycle, wdone the arbiter's write-complete pulse, g0 to g3 its grants and b0 to b3 its bus selects. posted is start AND we AND NOT amo. Held state: pst (1 bit), 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge, after reset: when posted is 1, pst becomes 1; otherwise when pst is 1 and wdone is 1, pst becomes 0; otherwise pst keeps its value. Outputs, combinational from the held state and the inputs: wdone_o is (wdone AND NOT pst) OR posted; go<k> (k from 0 to 3) is (g<k> AND NOT pst) OR (posted AND b<k>). Reset is synchronous and has priority.

blocks.name: pdev_bus
blocks.description: Combinational. The device decode and read multiplexer of the peripheral window (the 64 KB from 0x10010000), with the two PS/2 ports. pa (32 bits) is the access address, pw (1 bit) says a write is happening and pr (1 bit) says a read with side effects is happening. The device is chosen by bits 11:8 of pa: 0 is the GPIO, 1 the SPI master, 2 the I2C master, 3 the keyboard port, 4 the mouse port, anything else no device. gpio_we, spi_we, i2c_we, kbd_we and mouse_we are 1 when pw is 1 and the device is the one they are named for, and 0 otherwise. kbd_re and mouse_re are 1 when pr is 1 and the device is the keyboard port or the mouse port respectively, and 0 otherwise. prdata (32 bits) is the rdata input of the chosen device (gpio_rdata, spi_rdata, i2c_rdata, kbd_rdata or mouse_rdata), and 0 when no device is chosen. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: gpio_regs
blocks.description: The registers of a 16-pin GPIO. Held state: out (16 bits), oe (16 bits), ien (16 bits), pend (16 bits), and three 16-bit registers s1, s2 and prev that sample the input pins; all are 0 at reset. Each rising clock edge after reset: s1 becomes pins, s2 becomes s1 (held before the edge) and prev becomes s2 (held before the edge). rise is s2 AND NOT prev (held values, a pin that went from 0 to 1 in the synchronised signal). pend becomes (pend AND NOT clr) OR rise, where clr is wdata bits 15:0 when we is 1 and bits 3:2 of addr are 3 and 0 otherwise. When we is 1, bits 3:2 of addr choose a register to write with the low 16 bits of wdata: 0 is out, 1 is oe, 2 is ien, 3 is the write-one-to-clear of pend described above. rdata (32 bits, combinational on addr and the held state, whether or not we is 1) by bits 3:2 of addr: 0 is s2 in the low 16 bits, 1 is oe, 2 is ien, 3 is pend, each zero-extended to 32 bits. gpio_out is out and gpio_oe is oe (held values). irq is 1 when pend AND ien is not zero. Reset is synchronous and has priority.

blocks.name: spi_regs
blocks.description: The registers of an SPI master that moves one 8-bit word per transfer, between the bus and the master's word interface. Held state, all 0 at reset: cs (2 bits, the chip select chosen), last (8 bits, the last word received), done (1 bit), busy (1 bit), ien (1 bit). tx_cs is cs, tx_data is bits 7:0 of wdata, and tx_valid is 1 when we is 1, bits 4:2 of addr are 0 and tx_ready is 1 (a write of the word register starts a transfer when the master is ready, and is ignored otherwise). Each rising clock edge after reset: when tx_valid is 1, busy becomes 1; when rx_valid is 1 (the master finished a transfer), busy becomes 0, done becomes 1 and last becomes rx_data (rx_valid has priority over tx_valid for busy and over a clear for done). Independently of rx_valid and tx_valid, in every cycle: when we is 1 and bits 4:2 of addr are 2, cs becomes bits 1:0 of wdata; when we is 1 and bits 4:2 are 3, ien becomes bit 0 of wdata. In a cycle where rx_valid is 0, when we is 1 and bits 4:2 of addr are 1 and bit 1 of wdata is 1, done becomes 0. rdata (32 bits, combinational on addr and the held state) by bits 4:2 of addr: value 0: {24'b0, last}; value 1 (the status word): {30'b0, done, busy}, so bit 0 is busy and bit 1 is done; value 2: {30'b0, cs}; value 3: {31'b0, ien}; any other value: 0. A write of 1 to bit 1 clears done only in a cycle where rx_valid is 0. irq is 1 when done AND ien. Reset is synchronous and has priority.

blocks.name: i2c_regs
blocks.description: The registers of an I2C master that does one byte per command, between the bus and the master's command interface. Held state, all 0 at reset: last (8 bits, the byte of the last response), done, busy, nack, arb and ien (1 bit each). A write of the command register (we is 1 and bits 4:2 of addr are 0) with cmd_ready 1 gives cmd_valid 1; cmd_data is bits 7:0 of wdata, cmd_start is bit 8, cmd_stop is bit 9, cmd_nack is bit 10 and cmd_op is bits 12:11. cmd_valid is 0 when cmd_ready is 0 (the write is then ignored) or no such write happens. Each rising clock edge after reset: when cmd_valid is 1, busy becomes 1; when rsp_valid is 1, busy becomes 0, done becomes 1, last becomes rsp_data, nack becomes rsp_nack and arb becomes rsp_arb_lost (rsp_valid has priority over cmd_valid for busy and over a clear). Independently of rsp_valid and cmd_valid, in every cycle: when we is 1 and bits 4:2 of addr are 3, ien becomes bit 0 of wdata. In a cycle where rsp_valid is 0, when we is 1 and bits 4:2 of addr are 1 and bit 1 of wdata is 1, done, nack and arb become 0. rdata (32 bits, combinational on addr and the held state) by bits 4:2 of addr: value 0: {24'b0, last}; value 1 (the status word): {28'b0, arb, nack, done, busy}, so bit 0 is busy, bit 1 is done, bit 2 is nack and bit 3 is arb; value 2: 0; value 3: {31'b0, ien}; any other value: 0. A clear write (bit 1 of wdata set with bits 4:2 of addr equal to 1) has no effect in a cycle where rsp_valid is 1. irq is 1 when done AND ien. Reset is synchronous and has priority.

blocks.name: spi_m
blocks.description: SPI master: 8-bit words, mode 0, four chip selects

blocks.name: i2c_m
blocks.description: I2C master: one byte per command

blocks.name: irq_or2
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: irq_or3
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: irq_or3b
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ps2k_rx
blocks.description: The receiver of a PS/2 port. clk_i and dat_i (1 bit each) are the two lines. Held state: c1, c2, c3 (the clock line passed through three flip-flops), d1, d2 (the data line through two), all 1 at reset; cnt (4 bits, the bits received so far in the frame), sh (11 bits, the bits received, the first in bit 0), idle (16 bits, cycles since the last falling edge, saturating at 65535), and valid (1 bit), dout (8 bits) and perr (1 bit), all 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge, after reset: c1 becomes clk_i, c2 becomes c1, c3 becomes c2, d1 becomes dat_i, d2 becomes d1 (the values held before the edge); valid and perr become 0 unless set below. fall is 1 when c3 is 1 and c2 is 0 (a falling edge of the clock line). When fall is 1: idle becomes 0; bit cnt of sh becomes d2; and when cnt is 10 (this was the last bit of the frame) cnt becomes 0 and: if bit 0 of sh is 0 (start), d2 is 1 (stop) and the XOR of bits 9 down to 1 of sh is 1 (odd parity over the 8 data bits and the parity bit), valid becomes 1 and dout becomes bits 8:1 of sh; otherwise perr becomes 1; when cnt is not 10, cnt becomes cnt plus 1. When fall is 0: idle becomes idle plus 1 unless it is 65535; and when idle is 32767 (before the edge) cnt becomes 0 (a frame that stalled is dropped). The outputs valid, dout and perr show the held values.

blocks.name: ps2k_tx
blocks.description: The host-to-device transmitter of a PS/2 port. clk_i and dat_i (1 bit each) are the two lines, start (1 bit) starts a transmission of data (8 bits) when the transmitter is idle. Held state, all 0 at reset except as said: c1, c2, c3, d1, d2 (the lines through flip-flops as in a receiver: 1 at reset), st (2 bits: 0 idle, 1 inhibit, 2 sending), hold (14 bits), n (4 bits, falling clock edges seen since the request), sh (9 bits: the 8 data bits, bit 0 first, then the odd parity bit, which is 1 when the data has an even number of ones), done (1 bit) and err (1 bit). On each rising clock edge, after reset: c1 becomes clk_i, c2 becomes c1, c3 becomes c2, d1 becomes dat_i, d2 becomes d1; done becomes 0 unless set below. fall is 1 when c3 is 1 and c2 is 0 and rise is 1 when c3 is 0 and c2 is 1. State 0: when start is 1, sh becomes data followed by its parity bit, hold becomes 0, err becomes 0 and st becomes 1. State 1 (inhibit): hold becomes hold plus 1, and when hold is 16383 st becomes 2 and n becomes 0. State 2: when fall is 1, n becomes n plus 1 (n counts up to 12); when n is 12 and rise is 1: done becomes 1, err becomes d2 (1 when the device did not acknowledge by pulling the data line low) and st becomes 0. Outputs, combinational from the held state: clk_low is 1 in state 1 (the clock line is held low) and 0 otherwise; dat_low is 1 in state 2 when n is 0 or 1 (the start bit), or when n is from 2 to 10 and bit n minus 2 of sh is 0 (a 0 bit is sent by holding the line low); and 0 otherwise; busy is 1 when st is not 0; done and err show the held values.

blocks.name: ps2k_fifo
blocks.description: A first-in first-out queue of eight bytes. Held state, all 0 at reset: eight 8-bit registers q0 to q7 (q0 is the oldest byte) and the count cnt (4 bits, how many of them hold a byte). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when pop is 1 and cnt is not 0, the oldest byte leaves (q<k> becomes q<k+1> for k from 0 to 6, q7 becomes 0, and cnt goes down by 1); when push is 1 and the queue is not full (a byte that leaves in the same cycle counts as one free place), din joins it as the newest byte, after the bytes that were already there, and cnt goes up by 1. If both happen in one cycle, the pop is done first and then the push. When the queue is full and nothing leaves, push is ignored. head is q0 (combinational, 0 when cnt is 0) and count is cnt (4 bits, combinational).

blocks.name: ps2k_ctl
blocks.description: The registers of a PS/2 port, in the format of the Altera University Program PS/2 controller, around a receive queue that is a separate block: head (8 bits, the oldest received byte, 0 when the queue is empty) and count (4 bits, how many bytes wait) are inputs. Held state, all 0 at reset: re (1 bit, read interrupt enable) and ce (1 bit, command error). Other inputs: tx_busy, tx_done and tx_err from the transmitter; we is 1 for a store and re_pulse is 1 for a load, to the register chosen by bit 2 of addr (0 DATA, 1 CONTROL); wdata is the word stored. pop is 1 when re_pulse is 1 and bit 2 of addr is 0 (combinational). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when we is 1 and bit 2 of addr is 1, re becomes bit 0 of wdata and ce becomes 0; when tx_done is 1 and tx_err is 1, ce becomes 1. tx_start is 1 when we is 1, bit 2 of addr is 0 and tx_busy is 0, and 0 otherwise; tx_data is always bits 7:0 of wdata. rdata (32 bits, combinational): for bit 2 of addr 0: bits 31:16 are count, bit 15 is 1 when count is not 0, bits 7:0 are head, the other bits 0; for bit 2 of addr 1: bit 0 is re, bit 8 is 1 when re is 1 and count is not 0, bit 10 is ce, the other bits 0. irq is 1 when re is 1 and count is not 0.

blocks.name: ps2k_rxrst
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ps2m_rx
blocks.description: The receiver of a PS/2 port. clk_i and dat_i (1 bit each) are the two lines. Held state: c1, c2, c3 (the clock line passed through three flip-flops), d1, d2 (the data line through two), all 1 at reset; cnt (4 bits, the bits received so far in the frame), sh (11 bits, the bits received, the first in bit 0), idle (16 bits, cycles since the last falling edge, saturating at 65535), and valid (1 bit), dout (8 bits) and perr (1 bit), all 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge, after reset: c1 becomes clk_i, c2 becomes c1, c3 becomes c2, d1 becomes dat_i, d2 becomes d1 (the values held before the edge); valid and perr become 0 unless set below. fall is 1 when c3 is 1 and c2 is 0 (a falling edge of the clock line). When fall is 1: idle becomes 0; bit cnt of sh becomes d2; and when cnt is 10 (this was the last bit of the frame) cnt becomes 0 and: if bit 0 of sh is 0 (start), d2 is 1 (stop) and the XOR of bits 9 down to 1 of sh is 1 (odd parity over the 8 data bits and the parity bit), valid becomes 1 and dout becomes bits 8:1 of sh; otherwise perr becomes 1; when cnt is not 10, cnt becomes cnt plus 1. When fall is 0: idle becomes idle plus 1 unless it is 65535; and when idle is 32767 (before the edge) cnt becomes 0 (a frame that stalled is dropped). The outputs valid, dout and perr show the held values.

blocks.name: ps2m_tx
blocks.description: The host-to-device transmitter of a PS/2 port. clk_i and dat_i (1 bit each) are the two lines, start (1 bit) starts a transmission of data (8 bits) when the transmitter is idle. Held state, all 0 at reset except as said: c1, c2, c3, d1, d2 (the lines through flip-flops as in a receiver: 1 at reset), st (2 bits: 0 idle, 1 inhibit, 2 sending), hold (14 bits), n (4 bits, falling clock edges seen since the request), sh (9 bits: the 8 data bits, bit 0 first, then the odd parity bit, which is 1 when the data has an even number of ones), done (1 bit) and err (1 bit). On each rising clock edge, after reset: c1 becomes clk_i, c2 becomes c1, c3 becomes c2, d1 becomes dat_i, d2 becomes d1; done becomes 0 unless set below. fall is 1 when c3 is 1 and c2 is 0 and rise is 1 when c3 is 0 and c2 is 1. State 0: when start is 1, sh becomes data followed by its parity bit, hold becomes 0, err becomes 0 and st becomes 1. State 1 (inhibit): hold becomes hold plus 1, and when hold is 16383 st becomes 2 and n becomes 0. State 2: when fall is 1, n becomes n plus 1 (n counts up to 12); when n is 12 and rise is 1: done becomes 1, err becomes d2 (1 when the device did not acknowledge by pulling the data line low) and st becomes 0. Outputs, combinational from the held state: clk_low is 1 in state 1 (the clock line is held low) and 0 otherwise; dat_low is 1 in state 2 when n is 0 or 1 (the start bit), or when n is from 2 to 10 and bit n minus 2 of sh is 0 (a 0 bit is sent by holding the line low); and 0 otherwise; busy is 1 when st is not 0; done and err show the held values.

blocks.name: ps2m_fifo
blocks.description: A first-in first-out queue of eight bytes. Held state, all 0 at reset: eight 8-bit registers q0 to q7 (q0 is the oldest byte) and the count cnt (4 bits, how many of them hold a byte). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when pop is 1 and cnt is not 0, the oldest byte leaves (q<k> becomes q<k+1> for k from 0 to 6, q7 becomes 0, and cnt goes down by 1); when push is 1 and the queue is not full (a byte that leaves in the same cycle counts as one free place), din joins it as the newest byte, after the bytes that were already there, and cnt goes up by 1. If both happen in one cycle, the pop is done first and then the push. When the queue is full and nothing leaves, push is ignored. head is q0 (combinational, 0 when cnt is 0) and count is cnt (4 bits, combinational).

blocks.name: ps2m_ctl
blocks.description: The registers of a PS/2 port, in the format of the Altera University Program PS/2 controller, around a receive queue that is a separate block: head (8 bits, the oldest received byte, 0 when the queue is empty) and count (4 bits, how many bytes wait) are inputs. Held state, all 0 at reset: re (1 bit, read interrupt enable) and ce (1 bit, command error). Other inputs: tx_busy, tx_done and tx_err from the transmitter; we is 1 for a store and re_pulse is 1 for a load, to the register chosen by bit 2 of addr (0 DATA, 1 CONTROL); wdata is the word stored. pop is 1 when re_pulse is 1 and bit 2 of addr is 0 (combinational). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when we is 1 and bit 2 of addr is 1, re becomes bit 0 of wdata and ce becomes 0; when tx_done is 1 and tx_err is 1, ce becomes 1. tx_start is 1 when we is 1, bit 2 of addr is 0 and tx_busy is 0, and 0 otherwise; tx_data is always bits 7:0 of wdata. rdata (32 bits, combinational): for bit 2 of addr 0: bits 31:16 are count, bit 15 is 1 when count is not 0, bits 7:0 are head, the other bits 0; for bit 2 of addr 1: bit 0 is re, bit 8 is 1 when re is 1 and count is not 0, bit 10 is ce, the other bits 0. irq is 1 when re is 1 and count is not 0.

blocks.name: ps2m_rxrst
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: l2_ctl
blocks.description: Controller of the two mid-level caches (one per pair of harts, write-through) in front of the last-level cache controller. pair (1 bit) says which of the two arrays serves the request. The engine's request: rv is 1 in a cycle it is taken (only while ready is 1), rwe (write), rline (line access), raddr (32 bits), rwdata (32 bits) and rwstrb (4 bits). The arrays' answers for the address lk_addr: hit_a and hit_b (the line is present in array A, in array B) and line_a and line_b (256 bits, the 8 words of the line). The controller below: d_ready (it takes a request in a cycle where dv and d_ready are both 1), d_valid (1 for one cycle when its response is ready) and d_data (256 bits, the response). Held state, all 0 at reset: state (3 bits), we_q, line_q, pair_q, f_q (1 bit each), addr_q (32 bits), wd_q (32 bits), ws_q (4 bits), data_q (256 bits). States: 0 IDLE, 1 LOOK, 2 DREQ, 3 DWAIT, 4 FILL, 5 RESP (every other value acts as IDLE). Transitions on each rising clock edge, after reset: IDLE: when rv is 1, we_q, line_q, addr_q, wd_q, ws_q and pair_q take rwe, rline, raddr, rwdata, rwstrb and pair and state becomes DREQ when rwe is 1 (a write needs no lookup) and LOOK otherwise. LOOK: sel_hit is hit_b when pair_q is 1 and hit_a otherwise; when we_q is 0 and line_q is 1 and sel_hit is 1, f_q becomes 1 and state becomes RESP; otherwise f_q becomes 0 and state becomes DREQ. DREQ: when d_ready is 1, DWAIT. DWAIT: when d_valid is 1, data_q becomes d_data and state becomes FILL when we_q is 0 and line_q is 1, IDLE when we_q is 1 (a write is answered at once), and RESP otherwise. FILL: RESP. RESP: IDLE. Otherwise a state keeps its value. Outputs, from the held state and the inputs: ready is 1 in IDLE. resp_valid is 1 in RESP, and also in DWAIT when d_valid is 1 and we_q is 1. resp_data (256 bits) in RESP is 0 when we_q is 1; otherwise line_b when f_q is 1 and pair_q is 1, line_a when f_q is 1 and pair_q is 0, and data_q when f_q is 0; in every other state resp_data is 0. lk_addr is addr_q. dv is 1 in DREQ, with dwe we_q, dline line_q, daddr addr_q, dwdata wd_q and dwstrb ws_q (these four are always those values). fill_a_en is 1 in FILL when pair_q is 0 and fill_b_en is 1 in FILL when pair_q is 1; fill_addr is addr_q and fill_data is data_q, always. inv_en is 1 in IDLE when rv is 1 and rwe is 1 (a write removes its line from both arrays); inv_addr is raddr in IDLE and addr_q in every other state.

blocks.name: l3_ctl
blocks.description: Controller of the last-level cache (write-back, write-allocate: a write miss fills the line first) between the memory engine and the AXI4 master, beside its cache array. The engine's request: rv is 1 in a cycle it is taken (only while ready is 1), rwe (write), rline (line access), raddr (32 bits), rwdata (32 bits) and rwstrb (4 bits). The array's answers for the address lk_addr: hit (the line is present), lk_line (256 bits, the 8 words of the line, word 0 in bits 31:0), and, for a fill at lk_addr, vic_valid, vic_dirty, vic_addr (32 bits) and vic_data (256 bits) describing the line that would be replaced. The AXI4 master's: ax_ready (it takes a request in a cycle where ax_valid and ax_ready are both 1), ax_done (1 for one cycle when its transaction is complete) and ax_data (256 bits, the line it read). Held state, all 0 at reset: state (4 bits), we_q, line_q (1 bit each), addr_q (32 bits), wd_q (32 bits), ws_q (4 bits). States: 0 IDLE, 1 LOOK, 2 WBREQ, 3 WBWAIT, 4 FREQ, 5 FWAIT, 6 FILL, 7 WR, 8 AREQ, 9 AWAIT, 10 RESP (every other value acts as IDLE). Transitions on each rising clock edge, after reset: IDLE: when rv is 1, we_q, line_q, addr_q, wd_q and ws_q take rwe, rline, raddr, rwdata and rwstrb and state becomes LOOK. LOOK: for a read (we_q 0): hit gives RESP; without hit, vic_valid AND vic_dirty gives WBREQ and otherwise FREQ. For a write (we_q 1): hit gives WR; without hit, vic_valid AND vic_dirty gives WBREQ and otherwise FREQ (the line is brought in first). WBREQ: when ax_ready is 1, WBWAIT. WBWAIT: when ax_done is 1, FREQ. FREQ: when ax_ready is 1, FWAIT. FWAIT: when ax_done is 1, FILL. FILL: WR when we_q is 1, else RESP. WR: IDLE (the write is answered in WR itself). AREQ: when ax_ready is 1, AWAIT. AWAIT: when ax_done is 1, RESP. RESP: IDLE. Otherwise a state keeps its value. Outputs, from the held state and the inputs: ready is 1 in IDLE. resp_valid is 1 in RESP and in WR. resp_data (256 bits) in RESP is 0 for a write (we_q 1); for a read it is lk_line when line_q is 1 and otherwise lk_line word number addr_q[4:2] in bits 31:0 with the other bits 0; in every other state resp_data is 0. lk_addr is addr_q. fill_en is 1 in FILL, with fill_addr addr_q and fill_data ax_data. wr_en is 1 in WR, with wr_addr addr_q, wr_data wd_q and wr_be ws_q. ax_valid is 1 in WBREQ, FREQ and AREQ. ax_we is 1 in WBREQ and AREQ. ax_line is 1 in WBREQ and FREQ. ax_addr is vic_addr in WBREQ, addr_q with bits 4:0 cleared in FREQ, addr_q with bits 1:0 cleared in AREQ, and 0 in every other state. ax_wdata is wd_q and ax_wstrb is ws_q, always. ax_wline is vic_data, always.

blocks.name: la8_2
blocks.description: Combinational. y (256 bits) holds eight 32-bit addresses, the eight words of the 32-byte line that contains a (32 bits): word j (bits 32*j+31:32*j of y, j from 0 to 7) is a with bits 4:0 cleared plus 4*j (that is, bits 4:2 equal to j and bits 1:0 and 31:5 as in the line address). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: la8_3
blocks.description: Combinational. y (256 bits) holds eight 32-bit addresses, the eight words of the 32-byte line that contains a (32 bits): word j (bits 32*j+31:32*j of y, j from 0 to 7) is a with bits 4:0 cleared plus 4*j (that is, bits 4:2 equal to j and bits 1:0 and 31:5 as in the line address). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: h0_a
blocks.description: Combinational. b0 is bit 0 of y (8 bits). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: h0_b
blocks.description: Combinational. b0 is bit 0 of y (8 bits). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: h0_3
blocks.description: Combinational. b0 is bit 0 of y (8 bits). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: pair_or
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: l2_array_a
blocks.description: L2 for harts 0 and 1: 32 KB, 8 ways, write-through

blocks.name: l2_array_b
blocks.description: L2 for harts 2 and 3: 32 KB, 8 ways, write-through

blocks.name: l3_array
blocks.description: L3: 128 KB, 16 ways, write-back

blocks.name: c0_tlb_ilo
blocks.description: Translation lookaside buffer with 32 entries, fully associative. Each entry holds valid (1 bit), vpn (20 bits), ppn (22 bits), mega (1 bit) and flags (8 bits); flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. A pointer ptr (5 bits) names the entry the next fill writes. At reset every entry is invalid (all its fields 0) and ptr is 0. Lookup, combinational from the held entries and va (32 bits), whose page number is vpn = bits 31:12 of va: an entry matches when it is valid and, if its mega is 1, bits 19:10 of its vpn equal bits 19:10 of vpn (bits 31:22 of va), and if its mega is 0, its vpn equals vpn. When some entry matches, the lowest-numbered matching entry gives: hit 1; ppa (20 bits) is (bits 19:10 of its ppn, then bits 9:0 of vpn, which are bits 21:12 of va) when its mega is 1 and bits 19:0 of its ppn when its mega is 0; flags its flags. When none matches, hit, ppa and flags are 0. On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. flush is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. fill is 1: the entry ptr takes valid 1, vpn fill_vpn, ppn fill_ppn, mega fill_mega and flags fill_flags, and ptr goes up by one (wrapping from 31 to 0). Otherwise nothing changes.

blocks.name: c0_tlb_ihi
blocks.description: Translation lookaside buffer with 32 entries, fully associative. Each entry holds valid (1 bit), vpn (20 bits), ppn (22 bits), mega (1 bit) and flags (8 bits); flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. A pointer ptr (5 bits) names the entry the next fill writes. At reset every entry is invalid (all its fields 0) and ptr is 0. Lookup, combinational from the held entries and va (32 bits), whose page number is vpn = bits 31:12 of va: an entry matches when it is valid and, if its mega is 1, bits 19:10 of its vpn equal bits 19:10 of vpn (bits 31:22 of va), and if its mega is 0, its vpn equals vpn. When some entry matches, the lowest-numbered matching entry gives: hit 1; ppa (20 bits) is (bits 19:10 of its ppn, then bits 9:0 of vpn, which are bits 21:12 of va) when its mega is 1 and bits 19:0 of its ppn when its mega is 0; flags its flags. When none matches, hit, ppa and flags are 0. On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. flush is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. fill is 1: the entry ptr takes valid 1, vpn fill_vpn, ppn fill_ppn, mega fill_mega and flags fill_flags, and ptr goes up by one (wrapping from 31 to 0). Otherwise nothing changes.

blocks.name: c0_tlb_d
blocks.description: Translation lookaside buffer with 32 entries, fully associative. Each entry holds valid (1 bit), vpn (20 bits), ppn (22 bits), mega (1 bit) and flags (8 bits); flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. A pointer ptr (5 bits) names the entry the next fill writes. At reset every entry is invalid (all its fields 0) and ptr is 0. Lookup, combinational from the held entries and va (32 bits), whose page number is vpn = bits 31:12 of va: an entry matches when it is valid and, if its mega is 1, bits 19:10 of its vpn equal bits 19:10 of vpn (bits 31:22 of va), and if its mega is 0, its vpn equals vpn. When some entry matches, the lowest-numbered matching entry gives: hit 1; ppa (20 bits) is (bits 19:10 of its ppn, then bits 9:0 of vpn, which are bits 21:12 of va) when its mega is 1 and bits 19:0 of its ppn when its mega is 0; flags its flags. When none matches, hit, ppa and flags are 0. On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. flush is 1: every entry becomes invalid and ptr 0. fill is 1: the entry ptr takes valid 1, vpn fill_vpn, ppn fill_ppn, mega fill_mega and flags fill_flags, and ptr goes up by one (wrapping from 31 to 0). Otherwise nothing changes.

blocks.name: c0_ptw
blocks.description: Page-table walker for Sv32. Held state, all 0 at reset: st (IDLE 0, L1 1, L0 2), a (34 bits, the address of the entry to read), va (32 bits), fault (1), facc (1), fvpn (20). The address a is in RAM when bits 33:26 of a are 00100000. Outputs: busy is 1 when st is not IDLE. fault, fault_access and fault_vpn show the held fault, facc and fvpn exactly, as they are before the edge: they do not depend on this cycle's inputs (clear, start and the rest do not change them until the edge). When st is L1 or L0 and a is in RAM: req is 1 and addr is bits 31:0 of a; otherwise req and addr are 0. The entry read is pte = rdata (32 bits) when req and grant are both 1; its fields: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, ppn bits 31:10 (22 bits). fill is 1 when req is 1, grant is 1, V is 1, not (R is 0 and W is 1), (R or X) is 1, and not (st is L1 and bits 9:0 of ppn are not 0); then fill_vpn is bits 31:12 of va, fill_ppn is ppn, fill_mega is 1 when st is L1 (else 0), and fill_flags is bits 7:0 of pte. When fill is 0, fill_vpn, fill_ppn, fill_mega and fill_flags are 0. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 everything becomes 0 (IDLE). Otherwise first, when clear is 1: fault becomes 0 and a walk in progress is abandoned (st becomes IDLE; start is ignored on that edge; this is how a redirect cancels the walk of an instruction it squashed). Otherwise by st (fvpn is always bits 31:12 of the held va, never of vaddr): IDLE: when start is 1, va takes vaddr, a takes satp_ppn times 4096 plus (bits 31:22 of vaddr) times 4, fault becomes 0 and st becomes L1 (when start is 0 nothing else changes). L1 or L0 with a not in RAM, or with deny 1 (the physical memory protection refuses the read): st becomes IDLE, fault 1, facc 1, fvpn bits 31:12 of va. L1 or L0 with a in RAM and grant 0: nothing changes. L1 or L0 with a in RAM and grant 1, by pte: when V is 0, or R is 0 and W is 1: st IDLE, fault 1, facc 0, fvpn bits 31:12 of va. Else when R or X is 1 (a leaf): when st is L1 and bits 9:0 of ppn are not 0: st IDLE, fault 1, facc 0, fvpn bits 31:12 of va; otherwise st IDLE (the entry is delivered by fill). Else (a pointer) when st is L0, or when bit 7, bit 6 or bit 4 of pte (D, A, U: reserved in a pointer) is 1: st IDLE, fault 1, facc 0, fvpn bits 31:12 of va. Else (a pointer at L1): st becomes L0 and a takes ppn times 4096 plus (bits 21:12 of va) times 4.

blocks.name: c0_hart_memif
blocks.description: Combinational. The memory requests of one hart. core_req is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage asks for the bus. mmu_stall is 1 while the hart waits for a page-table walk, imiss is 1 while it waits for an instruction fetch to be refilled, ptw_req is 1 when the page-table walker wants a memory read, ifq is 1 when the fetch controller wants a line refill, and grant is 1 in a cycle when the memory system completes the hart's request. core_eff is core_req AND NOT mmu_stall AND NOT imiss (the core's own access is let through only when neither wait is active). req is core_eff OR ptw_req OR ifq. kind (2 bits) is 10 (binary) when ifq is 1, else 01 when ptw_req is 1, else 00. stall is mmu_stall OR imiss. run is NOT core_req OR grant. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_ifetch_ctl
blocks.description: Instruction-fetch refill controller of one hart, beside its instruction cache array. hit_lo and hit_hi say that the array holds the line of the word at lo_addr and of the word at hi_addr (the two words one fetch needs; the second only counts when need_hi is 1). hold is 1 while the hart waits for address translation (no fetch is judged then). miss_lo is NOT hit_lo; miss_hi is need_hi AND NOT hit_hi. imiss is (miss_lo OR miss_hi) AND NOT hold. Held state, all 0 at reset: ra (32 bits) and busy (1 bit). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when busy is 0 and imiss is 1, ra becomes the line-aligned address (bits 4:0 cleared) of lo_addr when miss_lo is 1, else of hi_addr, and busy becomes 1; when busy is 1 and done is 1, busy becomes 0; otherwise nothing changes. Outputs, from the held state and the inputs, before the edge: rq is busy. fill_en is busy AND done. rq_addr and fill_addr are ra. fill_data is line (256 bits, the memory's response; the word at ra in bits 31:0). inv_all is fence AND adv (the instruction cache is emptied when a fence.i instruction advances through the core). imiss as defined above.

blocks.name: c0_cat_lk
blocks.description: Combinational. y (64 bits) has a in bits 31:0 and b in bits 63:32. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_sp_lk
blocks.description: Combinational. lo is bits 31:0 of y (64 bits) and hi is bits 63:32 of y. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_sp_hit
blocks.description: Combinational. b0 is bit 0 of y (2 bits) and b1 is bit 1 of y. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_rload
blocks.description: Combinational. The value a load takes from the word the RAM read at its address. word (32 bits) is that word; memtype (3 bits) is the access type: 000 a byte, sign-extended; 001 a half-word, sign-extended; 010 a word; 011 a byte, zero-extended; 100 a half-word, zero-extended; 101 no access (the result is 0); 110 and 111 act as a word. addr (2 bits) is bits 1:0 of the access address (bits 1:0 are used): a byte is the byte at 8 times bits 1:0 of addr, a half-word is the half at 16 times bit 1 of addr. rdata (32 bits) is the result. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_en_and
blocks.description: Combinational. en is 1 when run is 1 and stall is 0, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_en_and_clr
blocks.description: Combinational. en is 1 when run is 1 and stall is 0, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_en_and_sf
blocks.description: Combinational. en is 1 when run is 1 and stall is 0, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_core_gate
blocks.description: Clock gate of one core. clk is the clock, en says whether the core may take the next clock edge, rst is the reset. A latch holds the value of (en or rst): it follows that value while clk is 0 and keeps it while clk is 1. gclk is clk and the latch value (so gclk is 0 whenever clk is 0, and while en and rst are both 0 it stays 0 and the core gets no edge). The reset forces the clock on so that a core whose en is not yet known is still reset. No state besides the latch.

blocks.name: c0_rsv_gate
blocks.description: Combinational. The set and clear of one core's load-reserved reservation, for a core that shares the bus with others. set_rsv and clr_rsv are the core's own strobes from its memory stage, self_grant is 1 when the core holds the bus this cycle (its access really happens). snoop_we is 1 when some core writes the RAM this cycle and addr (32 bits) is the address of that write. rsv_valid and rsv_addr (32 bits) are the core's held reservation. set is 1 when set_rsv is 1 and self_grant is 1, and 0 otherwise. clear is 1 when clr_rsv is 1 and self_grant is 1, or when snoop_we is 1, self_grant is 0, rsv_valid is 1 and bits 31:2 of addr equal bits 31:2 of rsv_addr; and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_amo_rsv
blocks.description: The reservation of load-reserved and store-conditional. set and clear are one-cycle strobes and addr is the 32-bit address of the access. Held state, all 0 at reset: rsv_valid (1 bit) and rsv_word (30 bits, the word address, addr bits 31:2, at the last set). On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1, rsv_valid and rsv_word become 0; otherwise when clear is 1, rsv_valid becomes 0 and rsv_word is unchanged; otherwise when set is 1, rsv_valid becomes 1 and rsv_word becomes addr bits 31:2. The outputs, from the held state only: rsv_valid is the held flag, and rsv_addr is a 32-bit value with rsv_word in bits 31:2 and 0 in bits 1:0.

blocks.name: c0_dcache_ctl
blocks.description: Controller of one hart's data cache (write-through, no write-allocate, loads allocate), beside its cache array. req is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage asks for the bus, is_ram is 1 when its address is in RAM, is_store is 1 for a store, is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction (load-reserved, store-conditional or read-modify-write), hit says that the array holds the line of addr (32 bits, the access address), hold is 1 while an earlier wait (page-table walk or instruction-fetch miss) is active. is_load is req AND is_ram AND NOT is_store AND NOT is_amo AND NOT hold (a plain RAM load that may be judged now). serve is is_load AND hit: the load is answered from the array and needs no bus transaction. dmiss is is_load AND NOT hit: the line must be refilled. Held state, all 0 at reset: ra (32 bits) and busy (1 bit). On each rising clock edge, after reset: when busy is 0 and dmiss is 1, ra becomes addr with bits 4:0 cleared and busy becomes 1; when busy is 1 and done is 1, busy becomes 0; otherwise nothing changes. Outputs, from the held state and the inputs, before the edge: rq is busy (a line read is wanted); rq_addr is ra; fill_en is busy AND done; fill_addr is ra; fill_data is line (256 bits, the memory's response). A completed RAM write is described by wdone (1 when a write completes this cycle), waddr (32 bits, its address), self (1 when the write is this hart's own) and w_plain (1 when it is a plain store, 0 when it is part of an atomic instruction). wr_en is wdone AND self AND w_plain (the cache array updates the word if it holds the line); wr_addr is waddr. inv_en is wdone AND NOT (self AND w_plain) (every other write, and every atomic's write, removes the line from this cache); inv_addr is waddr. No other output depends on the inputs not named for it.

blocks.name: c0_dc_rd
blocks.description: Combinational address decoder for the data side, in the memory stage. addr is the 32-bit address of an access. There are six regions that do not overlap, and every other address belongs to none. The RAM is the 64 MB from 80000000 to 83FFFFFF hexadecimal: bits 31:26 of addr are 100000. The CLINT is the 64 KB from 02000000 to 0200FFFF: bits 31:16 of addr are 0000001000000000. The PLIC is the 64 MB from 0C000000 to 0FFFFFFF: bits 31:26 of addr are 000011. The UART is the 4 KB from 10000000 to 10000FFF: bits 31:12 of addr are 00010000000000000000. The peripherals are the 64 KB from 10010000 to 1001FFFF: bits 31:16 of addr are 0001000000000001. The GPU is the 32 MB from 30000000 to 31FFFFFF: bits 31:25 of addr are 0011000. For instance 84000000 (just past the RAM) and 10001000 (just past the UART) is in no region, 10010000 is a peripheral, 31FFFFFC is the GPU and 32000000 is in no region. sel_ram, sel_clint, sel_plic, sel_uart, sel_periph and sel_gpu are 1 for the region addr is in and 0 otherwise; is_io is 1 when addr is in the CLINT, PLIC, UART, peripheral or GPU region. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_wfi_wake
blocks.description: Holds a hart's pipeline while it executes WFI (wait for interrupt), so an idle hart stops using the memory system, but gives up after a long wait. inst (32 bits) is the instruction in the memory stage. msip, mtip and meip (1 bit each) are the machine software, timer and external interrupt inputs of the hart; mip_sw (12 bits) are the pending bits software can set and mie (12 bits) the interrupt-enable bits. pend (12 bits) is mip_sw OR a word with bit 3 equal to msip, bit 7 equal to mtip, bit 11 equal to meip and every other bit 0. wait_on is 1 when inst is 0x10500073 (the WFI instruction) and pend AND mie is 0 (no enabled interrupt is pending). Held state: cnt (16 bits), 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge, after reset: when wait_on is 1, cnt becomes cnt plus 1 unless cnt is already 65535 (then it keeps its value); when wait_on is 0, cnt becomes 0. Reset is synchronous and has priority. Output, combinational from the held state and the inputs: hold is 1 when wait_on is 1 and cnt is not 65535.

blocks.name: c0_wfi_or
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_hold
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_or_ld
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_or_ifq
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_or_st
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_en_rq
blocks.description: Combinational. en is 1 when run is 1 and stall is 0, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_dsel
blocks.description: Combinational. The execute stage's result: y (32 bits) is from_fp when sel is 1 and from_alu when sel is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_dc_aq
blocks.description: Combinational. y (32 bits) is the OR of d<k> AND (all 32 bits replicated from sel<k>) for k from 0 to 3: the input of the hart whose select is 1, and the bitwise OR of the inputs whose selects are 1 when more than one is, and 0 when no select is 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_icache
blocks.description: Instruction cache: 32 KB, 2 ways, 32-byte lines, two lookup ports

blocks.name: c0_dcache
blocks.description: Data cache: 4 KB, 2 ways, 32-byte lines, write-through, one lookup port

blocks.name: c0_pc
blocks.description: Fetch-stage program counter. Holds the address of the instruction being fetched, always a multiple of two. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the held address becomes 80000000 hexadecimal, the first address of RAM; otherwise when trap_redirect is 1 it becomes trap_pc; otherwise when redirect is 1 it becomes redirect_pc; otherwise when stall is 1 it is left unchanged; otherwise it becomes the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0. trap_redirect comes from the write-back stage (an exception, an interrupt or mret) and so is older than redirect, which comes from the execute stage: when both are 1 the older one wins. is16 is 1 when the instruction being fetched is a 16-bit compressed instruction. pc is the held address. pc_plus4 is the address of the instruction after the one being fetched: the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0 (wrapping at 32 bits), available without waiting for a clock edge. trap_pc and redirect_pc are full 32-bit addresses and are loaded as they are, except that bit 0 of what is loaded is 0.

blocks.name: c0_if_id
blocks.description: IF/ID pipeline register. Sits between the fetch stage and the decode stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; inst_out becomes 32'h00000013, the instruction addi x0, x0, 0, which changes nothing (a bubble). Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A flush is how the instruction fetched on a wrong path is turned into a bubble. A further output, valid_out, is 0 after the register has been cleared (reset or flush) and becomes 1 at the first rising edge on which the register is loaded from its inputs (not cleared and not held); while stall holds the register, valid_out keeps its value. It tells the later stages that the instruction in this register is a real one and not a bubble.

blocks.name: c0_ctrl_decode
blocks.description: Combinational instruction decoder. Reads the 32-bit instruction word and drives every control signal in the design, plus the three register selector fields. The register selectors are plain slices of the instruction: rs1 is bits 19:15, rs2 is bits 24:20 and rd is bits 11:7. Every control output's meaning is given by its own encoding table; decode the instruction's opcode field (bits 6:0), funct3 field (bits 14:12) and bit 30 and drive each control output to the code that matches. Most instruction words are not valid instructions, so the unrecognised case is not an edge case: an instruction the decoder does not recognise must drive regwrite to NO_WRITE, memwrite to NO_STORE, brsel to NO_BRANCH, pcsel to NEXT and memtype to NO_ACCESS, so that it changes no architectural state and touches no memory. For an unrecognised instruction immsel, memsrc, alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care: with nothing written and no jump taken, nothing reads them. An opcode alone does not make an instruction valid. For an opcode whose funct3 values are listed (branch, load, store, the two arithmetic opcodes, and the register jump, whose only listed value is 000), a funct3 value that is not listed for it (a store with a width code that is not byte, half or word, for example) makes the instruction unrecognised, and the unrecognised case above applies, not the values the opcode's class would give. For the upper-immediate loads and the direct jump, bits 14:12 are part of the immediate, not a function code: they never make the instruction unrecognised, and the outputs do not depend on them. Bit 30 of the instruction word is read only where the funct3 table says so (subtract, and arithmetic shift right); under any other funct3 it is ignored and never makes an instruction unrecognised. The arithmetic unit's result is consumed in only three places: written back when memsrc is FROM_ALU, used as a data memory address, and used as the jump target for JUMPREG. An instruction that uses none of the three (a conditional branch, which compares through the branch comparator, an upper-immediate load, and a direct jump) does not use the arithmetic unit, so for it alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care. The add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction (opcode 0010111) is not an upper-immediate load: what it writes back is the address plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it does use the arithmetic unit, writes back FROM_ALU, and takes the immediate as its second operand. The register jump and link writes back the link address, the current address plus four, so it writes back FROM_PC; its jump target is the first register plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it also uses the arithmetic unit and takes the immediate as its second operand. The arithmetic unit's first operand is the register value for rs1, except for the add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction, whose first operand is the address of the instruction itself: asel is USE_PC for that instruction and USE_REGISTER for every other instruction that uses the arithmetic unit; where the arithmetic unit is not used asel is don't care. No clock, no reset, no state.

semantics.description: Whether this instruction writes a result back to a register.

encoding.0: NO_WRITE: the register file is left unchanged
encoding.1: WRITE: wdata is stored into the register selected by waddr

semantics.description: Which value is used as the arithmetic unit's second operand.

encoding.0: USE_REGISTER: the second operand is b_reg
encoding.1: USE_IMMEDIATE: the second operand is b_imm

semantics.description: Modifies two of the operation codes, mirroring how a real instruction set reuses one code for two related operations. Every other operation ignores it, and arith is 0 for those.

encoding.0: LOGICAL: SHIFT_RIGHT shifts in zeros, and ADD_SUB adds
encoding.1: ARITHMETIC: SHIFT_RIGHT replicates the sign bit, and ADD_SUB subtracts

semantics.description: Which operation the arithmetic unit applies to its two operands.

encoding.000: ADD_SUB: adds the operands, or subtracts the second from the first when arith is 1; the result wraps on overflow
encoding.001: SHIFT_LEFT: the first operand shifted left by the low five bits of the second, zeros shifted in
encoding.010: SET_LESS_THAN: 1 when the first operand is less than the second, both read as signed two's complement, otherwise 0
encoding.011: SET_LESS_THAN_UNSIGNED: 1 when the first operand is less than the second, both read as unsigned, otherwise 0
encoding.100: XOR: bitwise exclusive or of the operands
encoding.101: SHIFT_RIGHT: the first operand shifted right by the low five bits of the second; zeros shifted in when arith is 0, the sign bit replicated when arith is 1
encoding.110: OR: bitwise or of the operands
encoding.111: AND: bitwise and of the operands

semantics.description: Which immediate layout to extract from the instruction word, and how to extend it to 32 bits.

encoding.000: IMM_I: bits 31:20 of the instruction, sign-extended
encoding.001: IMM_S: bits 31:25 concatenated with bits 11:7, sign-extended
encoding.010: IMM_B: bit 31, bit 7, bits 30:25, bits 11:8, then a zero bit, sign-extended
encoding.011: IMM_U: bits 31:12 placed in the upper 20 bits, the low 12 bits zero
encoding.100: IMM_J: bit 31, bits 19:12, bit 20, bits 30:21, then a zero bit, sign-extended
encoding.101: NO_IMMEDIATE: the output is zero; this instruction has no immediate operand, and this is the code for it

semantics.description: Which comparison decides whether a branch is taken.

encoding.000: BR_EQ: taken when the operands are equal
encoding.001: BR_NE: taken when the operands differ
encoding.010: BR_LT: taken when the first is less than the second, both signed
encoding.011: BR_GE: taken when the first is greater than or equal to the second, both signed
encoding.100: BR_LTU: taken when the first is less than the second, both unsigned
encoding.101: BR_GEU: taken when the first is greater than or equal to the second, both unsigned
encoding.111: NO_BRANCH: never taken; this instruction is not a branch

semantics.description: The width and extension of a data memory access.

encoding.000: MEM_BYTE: one byte, sign-extended to 32 bits
encoding.001: MEM_HALF: two bytes, sign-extended to 32 bits
encoding.010: MEM_WORD: four bytes
encoding.011: MEM_BYTE_U: one byte, zero-extended to 32 bits
encoding.100: MEM_HALF_U: two bytes, zero-extended to 32 bits
encoding.101: NO_ACCESS: behaves as MEM_WORD; this instruction does not access data memory, and this is the code for it

semantics.description: Whether this instruction stores to data memory.

encoding.0: NO_STORE: memory is left unchanged
encoding.1: STORE: wdata is written at addr, in the width memtype selects

semantics.description: Which value is written back to the register file.

encoding.01: FROM_MEMORY: the value read from data memory
encoding.10: FROM_PC: the current address plus four, for a call
encoding.11: FROM_IMMEDIATE: the immediate, for an upper-immediate instruction

semantics.description: How the next program counter is chosen at the end of this instruction.

encoding.00: NEXT: the next address is the current address plus four
encoding.01: BRANCH: the next address is the current address plus imm when taken is 1, otherwise the current address plus four
encoding.10: JUMP: the next address is the current address plus imm, unconditionally
encoding.11: JUMPREG: the next address is jump_addr with its lowest bit forced to 0

semantics.description: Which value the arithmetic unit uses as its first operand.

encoding.0: USE_REGISTER: the first operand is the register value read for rs1
encoding.1: USE_PC: the first operand is the address of the instruction itself

blocks.name: c0_imm_gen
blocks.description: Combinational immediate generator. Extracts a field from the 32-bit instruction word and extends it to 32 bits, in the layout immsel selects; the meaning of each immsel code is given by its encoding table. Sign extension replicates the instruction's bit 31 into every bit above the extracted field. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_regfile
blocks.description: Register file.

blocks.name: c0_hazard_unit
blocks.description: Combinational hazard unit. Decides when the front of the pipeline must wait and when its instructions must be thrown away. rs1_id and rs2_id are the source register numbers in the instruction in the decode stage. rd_ex, regwrite_ex and memsrc_ex are the destination register, the write enable and the write-back source of the instruction in the execute stage; is_csr_ex is 1 when that instruction is a CSR instruction, whose result is only available in the write-back stage. redirect is 1 when the execute stage has decided to take a branch or a jump. md_busy is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage is a multiply or divide whose result is not ready yet. wb_redirect is 1 when the write-back stage is taking an exception or mret. A load is an instruction whose memsrc is FROM_MEMORY. The load-use condition is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage writes a register (regwrite_ex is 1) and is a load (memsrc_ex is FROM_MEMORY) or a CSR instruction (is_csr_ex is 1), rd_ex is not zero, and rd_ex equals rs1_id or rs2_id: the value is not yet available to the instruction behind it, which must wait one cycle. The unit does not look at whether the instruction in the decode stage really reads rs1 or rs2, so it may stall once when it did not need to; it never fails to stall when it should. stall is 1 when the load-use condition is 1 or md_busy is 1: the program counter and the IF/ID register hold. md_stall equals md_busy: the ID/EX register holds. flush_if_id is 1 when redirect is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: the instruction fetched after the branch, or after the instruction that is trapping, is on the wrong path. flush_id_ex is 1 when redirect is 1, wb_redirect is 1 or the load-use condition is 1: after a redirect the instruction in the decode stage is on the wrong path, and for a load-use a bubble must go into the execute stage. flush_id_ex does not depend on md_busy, because while a multiply or divide waits the instruction in the execute stage must stay where it is. flush_ex_mem is 1 when md_busy is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: a bubble goes into the memory stage while a multiply or divide works and when an exception or mret is taken. flush_mem_wb equals wb_redirect: the instruction in the memory stage must not commit. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: c0_id_ex
blocks.description: ID/EX pipeline register. Sits between the decode stage and the execute stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: is_amo_out becomes 0; amo_op_out becomes 0; irq_out becomes 0; pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; rs1_data_out becomes 0; rs2_data_out becomes 0; imm_out becomes 0; rs1_out becomes 0; rs2_out becomes 0; rd_out becomes 0; regwrite_out becomes 0, NO_WRITE; alusrc_out becomes 0; arith_out becomes 0; opsel_out becomes 0; asel_out becomes 0; brsel_out becomes 7, NO_BRANCH; pcsel_out becomes 0, NEXT; memtype_out becomes 5, NO_ACCESS; memwrite_out becomes 0, NO_STORE; memsrc_out becomes 0; mdop_out becomes 0, MD_NONE; valid_out becomes 0, a bubble; inst_out becomes 0; xcpt_out becomes 0, no exception; cause_out becomes 0; csrop_out becomes 0, CSR_NONE; is_csr_out becomes 0; is_mret_out becomes 0; csr_imm_out becomes 0. Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A cleared register holds a bubble: it writes no register, stores nothing, takes no branch, jumps nowhere, asks for no multiply or divide and raises no exception, whatever its other outputs read. A flush is used for the instruction behind a taken branch or jump, for the bubble after a load or CSR read that the next instruction needs, and when an exception or mret is taken. A stall holds the instruction in the execute stage while a multiply or divide is still working. valid is 1 for a real instruction and 0 for a bubble; xcpt is 1 when the instruction has raised an exception that will be taken when it reaches the write-back stage, with its cause in cause; csrop, csr_imm and is_csr say what a CSR instruction does; is_mret marks mret. A cleared register holds a bubble: valid, xcpt, csrop, is_csr and is_mret are 0. irq is 1 when the exception this instruction carries is really an interrupt that was attached to it in the decode stage (xcpt is then 1 too, and cause holds the interrupt's code); a cleared register holds irq 0. is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction and amo_op says which one (AMO_NONE for any other instruction); a cleared register holds is_amo 0 and amo_op 0.

blocks.name: c0_forward_unit
blocks.description: Combinational forwarding unit. Decides, for each of the two operands of the instruction in the execute stage, whether to use the value read in the decode stage or a newer value that is still on its way to the register file. rs1 and rs2 are the source register numbers of the instruction in the execute stage. rd_mem and regwrite_mem are the destination register number and write enable of the instruction in the memory stage; rd_wb and regwrite_wb are those of the instruction in the write-back stage. fwd_a is for the first operand (rs1) and fwd_b for the second (rs2); the meaning of each code is given by its encoding table. For each operand: when regwrite_mem is 1, rd_mem is not zero and rd_mem equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_EX_MEM; otherwise, when regwrite_wb is 1, rd_wb is not zero and rd_wb equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_MEM_WB; otherwise the code is FROM_REGISTER. The memory stage wins over the write-back stage because it holds the newer instruction. Register zero is never forwarded, because it reads zero whatever is written to it. No clock, no reset, no state.

semantics.description: Where an execute-stage operand comes from.

encoding.00: FROM_REGISTER: the value read from the register file in the decode stage, held in the ID/EX register
encoding.01: FROM_EX_MEM: the result held in the EX/MEM register, the value the instruction now in the memory stage will write back
encoding.10: FROM_MEM_WB: the write-back value, the value the instruction now in the write-back stage is writing to the register file
encoding.11: reserved: never produced

semantics.description: Where an execute-stage operand comes from.

encoding.10: FROM_MEM_WB: the write-back value, the value the instruction now in the write-back stage is writing to the register file
